raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# What does this PR do ?

With FP8 delayed scaling, we preemptively quantize the LoRA branch input to enable a fused RMSNorm + FP8 quant kernel and a [FP8 dropout+dequant kernel](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/2014). However, this does not generalize to more modern recipes like MXFP8 and NVFP4, so this PR removes this optimization.

Previous FP8 path:
```
-> RMSNorm+quant -> main GEMM -> ...
                \-> dropout+dequant -> LoRA A GEMM -> ...
```
Previous NVFP4 path:
```
-> RMSNorm -> quant -> main GEMM -> ...
                   \-> dequant -> dropout -> LoRA A GEMM -> ...
```
New path for both FP8 and NVFP4:
```
-> RMSNorm -> quant -> main GEMM -> ...
          \-> dropout -> LoRA A GEMM -> ...
```

# Changelog

- Stop pre-quantizing input to LoRA branch

# GitHub Actions CI

See the [CI section](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-running-github-ci) in the Contributing doc for how to trigger the CI. A Nvidia developer will need to approve and trigger the CI for external contributors.

# Before your PR is "Ready for review"

**Pre checks**:

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] Did you write any new necessary tests?
- [ ] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?
- [x] Does the PR affect components that are optional to install? (Ex: Numba, Pynini, Apex etc)
  - [ ] Reviewer: Does the PR have correct import guards for all optional libraries?

If you haven't finished some of the above items you can still open "Draft" PR.

# Additional Information
